chunks: Ja'far ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn al-Mugheera narrated to us from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his grandfather Abdullah ibn al-Mugheera, from Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Shu'ayri, from the Truthful Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, peace be upon them, who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The most steadfast in foot on the Path will be those who are most loving to my household.'

key_terms.أَثْبَتَكُمْ قَدَمًا: Most steadfast in foot, implying stability and certainty
key_terms.أَشَدُّكُمْ حُبًّا: Most loving, indicating the intensity of affection
key_terms.أَهْلِ بَيْتِي: My Household (Ahl al-Bayt), referring to the Prophet's family
key_terms.الصِّرَاط: The Path (Sirat), the bridge over Hellfire on the Day of Judgment

ai.seo_question: What determines one's steadfastness on the Path to Paradise according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in Fadail al-Shia, this hadith links the intensity of love for the Ahl al-Bayt to the degree of steadfastness on the Sirat, emphasizing that such love is not merely emotional but a criterion for spiritual success. In Shia tradition, this love is viewed as the practical manifestation of true faith, ensuring one's permanence on the path to Paradise.

en.badr-shahin: Ja’far bin Ali bin al-Hasan bin Ali bin Abdullah bin al-Mugheera narrated to us from his grandfather from his grandfather from Ismaeel bin Muslim ash-Shuairi from Ja’far bin Mohammed as-Sadiq (a) that the Prophet (sw) said:
The most sure-footed of you on the Path will be the most loving for my household.
